summary: The Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships fund a one-year master's at Oxford (100% of course fees plus a living grant of at least £21,805) for people from low- and middle-income countries, including Nigeria, and add a compulsory leadership programme with mentoring and networking. Winners are usually early-career professionals with a clear record of public service or socially minded enterprise who intend to return home and improve public life.
lookfor: Motivation and purpose: commitment to developing your country or community, with evidence of change you have driven
Leadership potential: initiative, strategic thinking, teamwork, communication, originality, willingness to take risks
Commitment to the Leadership Programme: full participation from before September to July
Clear link between your chosen course and your future professional work
An offer of a place on an eligible course (academic excellence)
cycle: For 2027-28: apply through the Oxford graduate form by your course's December 2026 or January 2027 deadline, ticking the scholarship and uploading the WH statement; shortlisted candidates are interviewed online, likely in April 2027; decisions expected by end of May 2027.

eligibility.q: Are you ordinarily resident in one of the eligible countries on Oxford's list (Nigeria and most of Africa are included)?
eligibility.no: Residents of the UK, USA, Canada and Australia are excluded. Consider Clarendon (no country restriction) instead.

eligibility.q: Are you applying to one of the eligible one-year master's courses (e.g. MPP, MSc Economics for Development, MSc Energy Systems, MSc Global Health Science and Epidemiology, BCL, MBA)?
eligibility.no: Doctorates and non-listed courses are not funded. Choose an eligible course or look at Clarendon or Rhodes.

eligibility.q: Do you intend to return to your country or region after the course and work to improve public life?
eligibility.no: This is a core requirement. If you plan to stay abroad long-term, look at merit-only awards such as Clarendon.

eligibility.q: Can you attend all Leadership Programme events, including events in Oxford before September?
eligibility.no: Participation is mandatory. If you cannot commit, do not tick this scholarship.

eligibility.q: Do you have some years of work experience in public service, policy, business or civil society?
eligibility.no: Not required, but the typical scholar has around 5 years' experience. Fresh graduates should show strong volunteer or community leadership.

steps.title: Check your country, course and commitment
steps.why: Only listed countries and courses qualify; applying for an ineligible course wastes your chance.
do: Open the official Oxford Weidenfeld-Hoffmann page (link below).
Find your country in the eligible countries list.
Find your course in the eligible courses list and copy its name exactly.
Read the Trust's eligibility flowchart and FAQs.
Write one sentence: 'After Oxford I will return to ___ to do ___.' If you cannot, rethink.
tips: Policy, development, health, environment, education and law courses dominate the list — pick the one that matches your work history.
avoid: Applying to a DPhil and expecting WH funding — only master's-level courses are funded.
check: My country and course are both on the 2027-28 lists.

links.t: Oxford: Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships and Leadership Programme

steps.title: Study the selection criteria
steps.why: The Trust selects for leadership and public-service purpose, not just grades. Every document should answer these criteria.
do: Open the Trust's 'Selection criteria' page.
Make a table with four columns: Motivation and purpose; Leadership potential; Commitment to the programme; Course relevance.
Under each, list 2–3 real examples from your life with numbers (people served, money raised, policy changed).
Read 3–4 scholar profiles on the Trust website to see the typical level.
tips: The Trust says it values the training more than the money — show you want the leadership programme, not only funding.
avoid: Treating this as a pure funding application.
check: I have at least two concrete examples for each criterion.

steps.title: Build your timeline and open the Oxford application
steps.why: The WH deadline is your course's December or January funding deadline. Transcripts, tests and references take weeks.
do: On your course page, open 'How to apply' and copy the deadline.
Create an account on the Oxford graduate application form and start an application for the course.
Set dates: referees asked (-60), transcript requested (-60), English test (-75), statements final (-14), submit (-7).
tips: Some eligible courses (e.g. MPP) have early December deadlines — check yours.
avoid: Assuming one fixed 'WH deadline' — it varies by course.
check: I have an account and a dated plan.

steps.title: Get transcripts, English evidence and passport ready
steps.why: You must win a place on the course first; incomplete applications fall behind.
do: Request an official (scanned, stamped) or interim transcript from your registry; get certified English translations if needed.

Check your course's English level; check whether you qualify for a waiver (English-taught degree completed within 2 years of your start date, or 2+ years' professional work in an English-speaking country).
If not, book IELTS or another accepted test so results arrive in time.
Check your passport is valid; renew at the Nigeria Immigration Service portal early if needed.
tips: Save every document as PDF under 4 MB with a clear name.
check: Transcript PDF ready; English plan confirmed.

steps.title: Write a CV that shows public impact
steps.why: Selectors look for proven leadership and impact; your CV is the quickest evidence.
do: Check the CV rules on your course page.
Order: Education; Professional experience (include NYSC and roles in government, NGOs or firms); Leadership and community work; Awards; Publications.
For each role write: problem, what you did, result with a number.
Export as PDF.
tips: Lead each bullet with a verb and end with a measurable outcome.
check: Each role shows at least one result.

steps.title: Write the course statement for your Oxford application
steps.why: You must be offered a place first. The department judges this statement.
do: Copy the statement type (personal statement or statement of purpose) and word limit from your course page.
Explain your academic preparation, the questions you want to study, and why this course fits.
Name specific modules or faculty.
End with your career goal and how the course serves it.
tips: Keep it consistent with your WH statement but do not copy it word for word.
avoid: Exceeding the limit — over-length statements are removed.
check: It answers the course page instructions exactly.
steps.prompt: As set by your course page.

steps.title: Complete the Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarship Statement
steps.why: This is the only document written for the Trust. It decides whether you are shortlisted for interview.
do: Download the 2027/28 WH Statement (Word) from the official Oxford WH page.
Read every question and word limit on the form itself; past versions asked short answers (around 200 words) on motivation, career plans and challenges.
For each answer use: context in your country, what you did, the result, what you learned, what you will do next.
Show how the course and the Leadership Programme will increase your impact at home.
Fill in the form, then save as PDF if the form asks; upload it in the Supporting documents section.
tips: 'Connect the dots' — link your past work, the course and your future public role in one story.
Name your country's specific problem (e.g. a policy, a health system gap) rather than 'Africa's challenges'.
avoid: Self-focused stories with no community impact.
check: I used the 2027/28 form and stayed within every limit.
Each answer has at least one concrete result.

links.t: Oxford WH page (download the 2027/28 statement here)

steps.prompt: Questions on the official 2027/28 WH Statement form: motivation, leadership, career plans and contribution to public life in your country.
steps.limit: As stated on the 2027/28 form — check the current guidance

steps.title: Line up three referees
steps.why: Oxford asks for three references; letters that confirm your leadership and public commitment support both the course and scholarship decisions.
do: Choose referees as your course page specifies (usually academic; some courses allow professional referees).
Ask 8 weeks ahead; send your CV, draft statements, the course name and deadline.
Register them in the References section with institutional emails and a deadline before yours.
Track them in the portal and remind them 10 days before.
tips: Ask at least one referee to describe a specific leadership example and its impact.

steps.title: Tick the scholarship and submit early
steps.why: You are only considered if you select Weidenfeld-Hoffmann in the Oxford scholarships section and upload the statement before the funding deadline.
do: In 'Qualifications, languages and funding' > Funding, select 'Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships and Leadership Programme'.
Upload the WH Statement in Supporting documents.
Check the ordinary-residence questions carefully.
Pay the application fee (£75 for taught courses; Nigeria is not on the fee-waiver list).
Submit and save the confirmation email.
tips: The scholarships section disappears after the funding deadline — submit a week early.
avoid: Forgetting the tick box — then you are not considered.
check: The WH scholarship is selected and the statement uploaded.

links.t: Watch: WHT Application Webinar: How to Apply to WHT (The Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Trust)
Watch: How to apply for a WHT scholarship (The Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Trust)

steps.title: Prepare for the online scholarship interview
steps.why: Shortlisted candidates are interviewed online, likely in April 2027. Interviewers push back on your answers.
do: Re-read your statements and CV.
Prepare 3 leadership stories (situation, action, result, lesson).
Prepare for policy questions on your country and sector; read recent news.
Learn the Trust's mission and programme parts (ethical leadership, business challenge, communication training).
Test camera, internet and a quiet, well-lit room; have a backup power and data source.
tips: Being persuasive and thoughtful matters more than perfection.
Do a mock interview with someone who will challenge you.
avoid: Generic answers about 'giving back' without a plan.
check: I can defend my career plan when challenged.

steps.title: Get the result and meet your offer conditions
steps.why: Decisions are expected by end of May 2027; you must also meet your course offer conditions.
do: Accept your course offer and note conditions.
If you have not heard by end of May 2027, assume you were not selected (no individual feedback is given).
If successful, you move to a partner college; send your final transcript by 31 August and your English score if required.
Apply for your UK Student visa once you have a CAS; plan to arrive for the pre-September events.
tips: Keep backup applications (e.g. Chevening, Commonwealth) open until results arrive.
avoid: Booking travel that clashes with mandatory Leadership Programme dates.
check: I know my conditions and programme dates.

faq.a: No. The typical scholar is an early-career professional with around five years of experience.
The award does not fund dependants, and UK rules now restrict dependants on taught master's visas unless government-funded.

faq.q: Do I apply to the Trust directly?
faq.a: No. You apply through the Oxford graduate application form by your course's funding deadline.

faq.q: Can I get WH for a DPhil?
faq.a: No. Only eligible master's-level courses are funded.

faq.q: Will I get feedback if unsuccessful?
faq.a: No. If not contacted by end of May 2027, assume you were not selected.
